detail: RemoteDisconnected: Remote end closed connection without response
RemoteDisconnected: Remote end closed connection without response

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the numbers and the record supports them, so this is decided on the arithmetic.

To the driver: you did arrive and you did wait, but not for long enough. The GPS trace runs from 17:15:00 to 17:19:00 — 25 stationary fixes (0.0 kph) about 24 m from the Plaza Singapura pin, comfortably inside the 120 m arrival radius for a LARGE_VENUE pickup — so the arrival test in POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are met, and the trip record's RIDER_NO_SHOW code with no boarding event meets limb (d). Limb (c) is where it fails. The continuous hold inside the geofence is 240 seconds (17:15:00 to 17:19:00) against a 300-second minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup: a 60-second shortfall. The clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from your 17:15:20 'arrived' tap, but even on the tap clock (17:15:20 to the 17:19:00 cancellation) the wait is 220 seconds, 80 seconds short. Nothing rescues that: POL-NS-05 does not fire (you were stationary, ~24 m away, not over 300 m out and not at 15 kph), POL-NS-03 does not apply (you were inside the arrival radius, not outside it), and POL-NS-04 does not apply (no locating message from the rider). Under POL-NS-06 a dwell short of the minimum means the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied — the waiting period is what the fee buys. The one route to summing separate in-geofence intervals, limb (i), needs a present and populated traffic advisory, and EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so there is nothing to sum; in any event the trace shows a single interval only.

To the rider: the refund does not depend on where you were. I note the rider track places your device about 519 m from the pin with no qualifying in-radius fixes; that would have defeated POL-NS-04, and it does not matter here, because POL-NS-06 turns on the driver's own fixes.

The amount is not in dispute. The fare breakdown's cancellation-fee line of SGD 8.00 is the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00) — the vehicle tier produced it — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect, and the whole SGD 8.00 is refunded. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and POL-NS-06 displaces it here (the anti-farming check would not have tripped in any event — 1 no-show termination in 30 days against 120 completed trips).

Nothing escalates. No POL-NS-08 limb applies (arrival marker 20 seconds from the nearest fix, no trace gaps, all 3 chat messages present, the fee reconciles), and no POL-NS-09 trigger fires (no contradicting artifacts, no counterparty dispute history, no anti-farming trip, no impaired sole evidence). Your statement that you were at the marked bay and the rider did not appear is consistent with the trace, but a rider's absence does not make a short wait chargeable. No clause produces a referral, and no profile field was used as a ground against either party.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider and driver: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded in full. The driver's 'arrived' event is recorded at 2026-09-04T07:25:20, but the GPS trace places the driver 559.37 m from the pickup pin at every recorded fix, against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius in POL-NS-02. There are zero qualifying in-geofence fixes, and the longest qualifying run and accumulated dwell are both 0 seconds against the 300-second minimum. POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) therefore fail and the fee is not chargeable. I accept the rider's claims under POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06, and the driver's own concession that the proximity and dwell limbs are not met. The driver's point that he stayed stationary does not help him: he stayed stationary 559.37 m away, outside both the arrival radius and the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling, so POL-NS-03 does not apply. The rider's absence from the pin at 519.46 m and the absence of any rider chat message do not defeat the refund, because POL-NS-06 refunds a short waiting period whether or not the rider was present or responded. The driver's anti-farming point is accepted but irrelevant: POL-NS-07 compensation requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, which it is not, so no driver compensation is payable. The fare breakdown's SGD 4.00 cancellation fee reconciles with the fee_schedule — the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee of SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of SGD 4.00 — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. The MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09104-01 carries weight 0.0 and cannot extend the waiting clock; it does not carry the deciding fact. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger applies. Because the arrival marker was false and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists, POL-NS-05(ii) also requires the false-arrival referral included above.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii): record trip TRP-09104 as a false-arrival event against driver DRV-09104; the arrival marker at 2026-09-04T07:25:20 is false because the GPS trace places the driver 559.37 m from the pickup pin.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-09105 is refunded in full to the rider, and no compensation is payable to the driver.

Why the fee does not stand. The driver's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-09105) places him stationary at 219.77 m from the Tower B pickup pin for the entire record — 34 fixes from 13:05:00 to 13:10:30, speed 0.0 kph, trace distance 0.0 km, and zero fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius (qualifying_fix_count 0, longest qualifying run 0.0 s). Under POL-NS-02 the driver is not deemed to have ARRIVED at the pickup point, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the fee is not chargeable. This is a wrong-entrance arrival governed by POL-NS-03: the driver was stationary outside the arrival radius but inside the 400 m ceiling (219.77 m), and held that position for 330 seconds, longer than the 300-second LARGE_VENUE dwell, so POL-NS-03 refunds the cancellation fee in full. Independently, the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second minimum — a 300-second shortfall — which under POL-NS-06 also makes the fee non-chargeable whether or not the rider was present.

Fault lies with the driver, so no compensation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-09105) shows the rider naming the sub-location — 'I am at Tower B ride-hail pickup' at 13:05:05 and 'That is the other entrance. Please come to Tower B.' at 13:06:35 — while the driver replied only that he was 'waiting at the mall taxi stand' at 13:06:00 and never moved before cancelling at 13:10:30. The driver's own filed statement concedes he 'did not move to Tower B'. Under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation, so the POL-NS-07 payment of 80% (SGD 3.20 of SGD 4.00) is not payable. The driver-side claim that this is a wrong-face-of-same-venue case is accepted, but it leads to the same result: the fee is refunded and, because the rider specified the tower, limb (ii)'s pin-ambiguity goodwill of SGD 2.00 does not apply either.

The arrival marker is not false. At the 13:05:20 marker the driver was 219.77 m from the pin — inside POL-NS-05's 300 m trigger — and at 0.0 kph, below its 15 kph trigger, so POL-NS-05 does not engage at all; POL-NS-05 expressly sends a driver stationary within 300 m but outside the arrival radius to POL-NS-03. No false-arrival referral under POL-NS-05(ii) is entered against the driver. The rider's POL-NS-04 argument reaches the same outcome (full refund, no compensation) and changes nothing; on its own terms it is also doubtful, since the driver replied at 13:06:00 to the rider's 13:05:05 locating message, inside the 120-second window.

Amount. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-09105) itemises the cancellation fee as the only chargeable line — base_fare 0.00, platform_fee 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00, tolls 0.00, total_charged SGD 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. SGD 4.00 is also the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under fee_schedule.resolution_rule, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the full refund is SGD 4.00.

Integrity and escalation. The trace has 100% coverage, 34 fixes, no gaps and rider_track present; the chat log holds 4 messages matching trip_record.chat_message_count; the arrived 13:05:20 event matches the trace cadence. No limb of POL-NS-08 is engaged, no two artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, and no POL-NS-09 trigger fires (the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is not in play because the fee itself does not stand). Confidence is above the 0.70 floor. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09105-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0) and its absence cannot be used to sum separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i); it carries nothing and does not affect the outcome.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both parties should read this. The disputed SGD 6.00 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider.

The facts are largely agreed and the platform's own records settle them. The driver did reach the pickup: the trip record shows an 'arrived' event at 18:20:20 and a driver-side termination at 18:25:30 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, and the GPS trace places all 34 of his fixes 24.01 m from the Tampines MRT Exit D private-hire bay — well inside the 150 m arrival radius for a TRANSPORT_HUB. Measured as POL-NS-01(c) requires, from the first in-geofence fix at 18:20:00 and not from the arrival tap, he held position for 330 seconds, 30 seconds over the 300-second minimum, with no gap and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. So the driver's account that he waited inside the geofence is corroborated, and there is no false-arrival marker under POL-NS-05.

That does not decide the case. POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider where three things hold together, and all three do. (a) The rider sent two locating messages inside the waiting window: 'I am at Exit D under the green sign. Where is your car?' at 18:21:00 and 'I still cannot see you. Please reply.' at 18:23:25. (b) The driver never answered: the 120-second window opened by the 18:21:00 message closed at 18:23:00 with no reply, trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, and no in-app voice call was made at any point before the 18:25:30 cancellation. (c) The rider's device was at the pickup: all 16 of its fixes qualify, spanning 18:20:30 to 18:25:30, at a mean reported distance of 41.9 m, inside the 200 m presence radius for a TRANSPORT_HUB. The rider was where they were supposed to be and was actively trying to coordinate; the silence was the driver's.

POL-NS-04 is one of the clauses POL-NS-01 itself names as displacing its baseline charge. Because it applies, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, and the clause states no driver compensation is payable. The driver's POL-NS-07 claim to 80 percent (SGD 4.80) therefore fails — not because the arrival and dwell findings are wrong, which they are not, but because POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. The driver's own submission correctly identified POL-NS-04 as the exposure. The POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance route does not apply either: 24.01 m is inside the arrival radius, not the 400 m band outside it, so no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises.

I have checked the escalation triggers and none fires. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0; both disputes_with_counterparty_90d counters are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not met; and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test does not trip — 1 no-show termination against 120 completed trips, below both the '4 or more' count and the 0.08 rate. The lifetime prior_no_show_flags counters (2 on the driver, 1 on the rider) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carry nothing here. No two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence.

The SGD 6.00 refunded is the cancellation_fee line on the fare breakdown (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), which reconciles with the fee schedule: the GREATER of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_PLUS vehicle-tier fee (SGD 6.00). No artifact is impaired on any limb of POL-NS-08 — 20 seconds of clock skew against the 90-second limit, no sampling gap and 34 fixes against the 6-fix floor, 3 chat messages matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 3 with an unbroken msg_id sequence, and a cancellation line equal to the schedule figure — so the finding rests on full-weight evidence. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09106-01, weight 0.0) is relied on by neither side and has no bearing; the driver needed no accumulated-dwell extension, as his 330 seconds is a single continuous run.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both parties read the same timeline; what divides you is whether the two spells inside the pickup geofence may be added together. Rider: the car left the bay at 19:02:50 and came back at 19:03:50, so the longest continuous hold was 170 seconds — 130 seconds short of the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum — and POL-NS-06 should return the SGD 4.00 fee. That reading would be right if the two spells had to stand alone, but POL-NS-06(i) permits them to be summed, and both of its conditions are met. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09107-01 is present and populated, type CLOSURE, active 18:50–19:30 over the whole waiting window, its geometry covering the marked ride-hail bay, and its own description records that the temporary kerb closure required pickup vehicles to circulate before returning to the bay. The driver's furthest point during that single circulation was 179.8 m from the pin, inside the 300 m leash. The runs of 170 s (19:00:00–19:02:50) and 160 s (19:03:50–19:06:30) therefore total 330 seconds, 30 seconds above the 300-second minimum. I therefore reject the rider's central claim that the waits must not count together, and the related claim that the limb (i) premise is unestablished. The driver's own message at 19:04:05 that he was 'back at the marked bay now' does not defeat limb (i): the closure required one circulation and a return to a lawful bay, which is exactly the situation the limb accommodates. On the other side, the rider is right that rider presence is not an element of the shortfall route and that the rider track 519 m from the pin assists nobody — but the shortfall route is not reached, so rider absence decides nothing. All four POL-NS-01 limbs hold: the arrived event at 19:00:20; 35 qualifying fixes inside the 120 m arrival radius; 330 seconds of accumulated dwell; driver-terminated with RIDER_NO_SHOW at 19:06:30 with no boarding event. Nothing in POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces them — the arrival marker was not false (the driver was stationary inside the radius, so POL-NS-05 does not bite), POL-NS-03 does not govern because the driver was inside the radius rather than merely within 400 m of it, and POL-NS-04 fails for want of any rider locating or coordinating message. The fare reconciles: the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee of SGD 4.00 equals the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of SGD 4.00 and the charged cancellation-fee line is SGD 4.00, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged, and both profiles being at 1 and below threshold the anti-farming check on no_show_terminations_30d does not trip. Outcome: the SGD 4.00 charge stands; under POL-NS-07 the driver is paid 80 percent of it — SGD 3.20 of SGD 4.00 — and under POL-GEN-03 the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd mirroring the compensation figure. No referral fires: POL-NS-05(ii) requires a false arrival marker, which this was not, and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: The driver's baseline no-show case is made out on the merits. EV-TRIP-09108 shows an arrived event at 09:30:20; EV-GPS-09108 places the driver 24.01 m from the PLQ pin, inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, with 34 qualifying fixes; the dwell from the first in-geofence fix at 09:30:00 to the 09:35:30 cancellation is 330 seconds, over the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum; and the trip was terminated by the driver with RIDER_NO_SHOW after the dwell elapsed. POL-NS-05 is not triggered: the driver was stationary at 0.0 kph and 24.01 m from the pin, so the arrival marker is not false. POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver was inside the POL-NS-02 radius. POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to excuse, and the missing advisory EV-ADVIS-09108-01 (weight 0.0) is not engaged. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: limb (a) fails because the chat log contains no rider locating or coordinating message; I note that the rider track has 0 qualifying fixes, so limb (c) would be undecidable/neutral rather than affirmatively failed, but the clause does not apply without limb (a). The SGD 4.00 fare line is correct as the greater/tie of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee. However, POL-NS-07's anti-farming check trips: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 7 (4 or more) and 7 / 70 completed trips = 0.10, above 0.08. Compensation is therefore withheld and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d). Escalation is terminal: no monetary ruling issues, and the SGD 4.00 fee is held rather than collected or refunded. The escalation packet must direct the reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.00 fee in full under POL-NS-07, recorded as a referral. The rider's pattern-review request is answered by the driver-profile anti-farming trigger; the rider's no-show dispute count and same-pair dispute count are 0, so no rider-abuse escalation limb fires. Confidence is 1.0 because the deciding facts come from platform telemetry with no disclosed impairment; the missing advisory is weight 0.0 but does not carry the escalation fact.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-07: Direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in full; the SGD 4.00 fee is held pending review.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the SGD 6.00 no-show cancellation fee cannot be confirmed or returned on this record. The case goes to a human reviewer, and the SGD 6.00 is held rather than collected or refunded.

WHY NEITHER SIDE WINS THE ARRIVAL LIMB. POL-NS-01 charges a no-show fee only if all four limbs hold, and limbs (b) and (c) read the GPS trace. Limb (a) is met: EV-TRIP-09109 carries the driver's 'arrived' marker at 2026-09-09T21:10:20. Limb (d)'s reason code is met: the trip was ended by the driver at 21:15:40 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW. But the GPS trace for this trip, EV-GPS-09109, is MISSING: payload null, weight 0.0. With no fix of any kind there is no way to place the driver inside the 150 m arrival radius for this TRANSPORT_HUB pickup (POL-NS-02 and fee_schedule.arrival_radius_m), and no way to measure the 300-second in-geofence dwell POL-NS-01(c) requires. That clause expressly runs the dwell clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the arrival tap, so the record's wait_time_min 5.3 (320 seconds from tap to cancellation) does not supply it. Limbs (b) and (c) are therefore undecided, not failed.

TO THE RIDER: your reading of POL-NS-02 - that a trace containing no in-radius fix means the driver 'never arrived' and the whole fee is refunded - does not apply here. That clause refunds on a finding of absence drawn from a trace that exists. A trace that is missing or unusable is an impaired artifact under POL-NS-08(b), and an impaired test leaves the arrival limb undecided rather than failed. An undecided limb supports neither the fee (which the driver needs) nor the full refund of SGD 6.00 (which you need). Your POL-NS-06 shortfall route fails for the same reason - no dwell can be computed, so no shortfall can be found - and its limb (i) aggregation route is closed because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09109-01 is also MISSING (payload null, weight 0.0). POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-05 each run off the missing trace and cannot be run: POL-NS-03 needs stationary fixes outside 150 m but within the 400 m ceiling, and POL-NS-05 needs a fix matched to the arrival timestamp before the marker can be tested. You are right that the driver's chat line 'I am at the private-hire bay' (21:10:40) is a bare assertion of position and that a MISSING artifact carries no fact (POL-GEN-02).

TO THE DRIVER: your chat messages ('I am at the private-hire bay' at 21:10:40, 'I am here beside the sign' at 21:11:45) and your counter-statement that you held the bay for the full waiting period are evidence, but they stand in for the GPS test the clause actually sets, and where that test admitted no reading at all an account in its place neither establishes the limb nor lifts the confidence cap. POL-NS-07 compensation of SGD 4.80 (80 percent of SGD 6.00, per the policy's own worked example) is therefore not payable, because it requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full. The anti-farming check does not trip in any event: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against a floor of 4, and 1/120 = 0.008 against a rate floor of 0.08. driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags (2) is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 makes context only and may not be substituted for the trailing-30-day field.

NO FARE DEFECT. The charge itself reconciles: SGD 6.00 is the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), which is exactly what EV-FARE-09109 itemises as cancellation_fee, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. The chat log is complete (4 messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count 4), so POL-NS-08(c) is not engaged. POL-NS-04 does not apply because the driver replied inside 120 seconds (rider 21:11:30, driver 21:11:45).

OUTCOME. Escalation is required under POL-NS-09(e), because the sole evidence for the deciding fact - in-geofence presence and dwell - is the missing trace, impaired under POL-NS-08(b), and under POL-NS-09(a), because confidence is capped by that artifact at weight 0.0, far below the 0.70 floor. Escalation is terminal, so no money issues and the SGD 6.00 stays on hold. Open question for the reviewer: obtain a usable driver GPS export (or other reliable location record) covering roughly 20:55 to 21:16 on 2026-09-09, to determine whether the driver entered the Woodlands MRT private-hire bay geofence and held position inside it for 300 continuous seconds before cancelling at 21:15:40.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both of you agree on the underlying arithmetic, and so do I. The driver's arrival marker at 06:50:20 is corroborated by the GPS trace: the first in-geofence fix at 06:50:00 sits about 24 m from the pickup pin, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (POL-NS-02), and the trace shows a single unbroken in-geofence hold of 330 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum (POL-NS-01(c)), with the trip ended by the driver at 06:55:30 under RIDER_NO_SHOW after that dwell elapsed and no boarding event (POL-NS-01(d)). The rider's own track places her 519.4 m from the pin throughout and the driver replied to her message within 120 seconds, so POL-NS-04 does not apply, and POL-NS-03, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 do not apply either. On the merits the SGD 4.00 fee is chargeable, the anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination against 120 completed trips in 30 days, below both the count of 4 and the rate of 0.08), and absent anything else the driver would be owed SGD 3.20 (80% of SGD 4.00) under POL-NS-07.

This case cannot be decided here. POL-NS-09(c) requires escalation where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. Both counters read 2, and the rider's own filing describes this as 'another dispute with the same driver.' The trigger is met, and escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal: it replaces any monetary outcome, so no refund and no compensation issue. The SGD 4.00 sits at payment_status PENDING and is HELD — not collected from the rider, not refunded to her — until a human reviewer resolves it.

The open question for the reviewer is the repeat pattern between this rider and this driver: whether the earlier disputes in the 90-day window concern the same conduct, and whether the SGD 4.00 no-show fee should stand or be refunded in light of that history.

Two items do not change the outcome. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0); the rider cited it only for its absence, which closes the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation route but decides nothing, since the single 330-second hold already meets the minimum. The rest of the bundle is clean under POL-NS-08: no clock skew (20 s), no trace gap (34 fixes, 0 s maximum gap, rider_track present), the chat log reconciles (4 messages against chat_message_count 4), and the SGD 4.00 line matches the fee_schedule resolution rule (the greater of the SGD 4.00 STANDARD zone-class fee and the SGD 4.00 RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee). The driver's anti-farming argument rests only on the citable counters no_show_terminations_30d and completed_trips_30d; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is context only and was properly not used.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: this dispute turns on whether the trip ran longer than the route shown at booking, and the answer is measured, not argued. The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-09112) records 11.5 km against the booked optimal route of 10.0 km (EV-TRIP-09112), an excess of 1.5 km — 15.00% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both tests must pass. Here the 1.5 km excess clears the 0.8 km limb but fails the percentage limb (15.00% is below 20%), so no deviation is established on this trip and no distance refund is available under POL-RD-02. The rider's own advocate correctly concedes this gate; the 1.5 km figure the rider quotes is real, but it does not reach the threshold the policy sets. The rider's arithmetic (charged total 19.39 less a recomputed fare of 17.70 = 1.69) is correct in itself, but POL-RD-02 only runs once a deviation is established, so that sum does not become payable, and no amount is refunded.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
ruling.explanation_continued: The trace supporting the measurement is unimpaired: EV-GPS-09112 covers 100% of the trip with 133 fixes, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix interval of 0.0 s, so it meets no impairment limb (a)–(c) of POL-RD-07 and no corroboration question arises. The driver's statement that he stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop, and the rider's in-app message that the trip looked a little longer, do not change the measurement — neither identifies a rider-requested detour nor an exculpatory traffic event. The traffic advisory artifact (EV-ADVIS-09112-01) carries no payload and can carry no fact, but since no deviation is established there is nothing for it to excuse. No billing-integrity correction applies under POL-RD-09(4): the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines (tolls_erp 0.00) and no airport surcharge (0.00). No driver compensation arises under POL-RD-04: the distance charged (11.5 km) is not less than the 11.5 km the trace records, so the unbilled-shortfall limb is not met. No repeat-deviation pattern engages POL-RD-06 (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 610 completed trips in 90 days). No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: trip_id TRP-09112 matches across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, the trace is unimpaired, timestamps are consistent, and every charge line has a counterpart. Outcome: NO_ACTION — the filing party's claim is not supported by the evidence on the threshold test, and the present payment state (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) stands unchanged. The confidence is 0.95, the deciding facts being carried by artifacts at full weight (EV-GPS-09112 and EV-TRIP-09112).

ruling.explanation:
Rider, you and the driver agree the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector was closed; the argument is only how far the closure justifies the detour. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-09113) is unimpaired - 205 fixes at 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps - so it governs: the trip ran 18.0 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km (EV-TRIP-09113), an excess of 8.0 km (80%).

The closure excuses only part of that. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is the lower of the 8.0 km measured and 1.30 x (12.0 km shortest lawful alternative - 10.0 km booked optimal) + 1.00 km tolerance = 3.60 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km over 27.2 minutes (the booked 20.0 minutes scaled by 13.60/10.00; amended_optimal_duration_min is null). That leaves 4.40 km of unexcused excess - 32% of the adjusted optimal - a deviation, but not a MATERIAL one. So the POL-RD-06 profile check, its FULL_REFUND uplift and its conduct referral do not apply; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 610 completed trips, far below the pattern test, and the derived 'material' status on the trace was computed on the pre-adjustment 8.0 km the clause tells us to set aside.

Driver, your POL-RD-04 argument that the rider asked for the detour does not run. The rider's reply 'please take the lawful diversion' names no road, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so the corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and what the rider authorised was the lawful 12.0 km diversion the advisory records - not the 18.0 km driven. Your counterparty statement that the closure 'forced a diversion' adds nothing beyond the advisory, whose own arithmetic caps the exoneration at 3.60 km.

Refund under POL-RD-02 (METERED fare): recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 surge (read from EV-FARE-09113) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP lying on the optimal route = 23.416. Charged total 31.42. Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05 - about 25% of the charge, so a partial refund, not a full one.

ERP. The 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' line is off-route ERP and is ALREADY COMPREHENDED in the 8.05, because the recomputed fare carries only the on-optimal-route gantry; it is itemised for transparency and never added on top (POL-RD-09(1)). The 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' line is different: it is a charge for a gantry the trace never passes - the nearest fix is 834 m away, outside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 sets - so it is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), and that correction is referred.

Total refund: 8.05 + 1.00 = SGD 9.05. No driver compensation is due: the fare billed the full 18.0 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall, and no repeat-deviation pattern exists. Profiles were used only for the tests POL-GEN-01 permits. Confidence 0.9 - every artifact carrying a deciding fact is at full weight.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP line is a charge for a gantry the GPS trace never passes (nearest of 205 fixes 834 m away, outside the 250 m match radius) and has been refunded as a standalone correction; refer the line for billing-integrity review.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and Driver: I am refunding the SGD 3.20 ERP line and leaving the rest of the fare as charged. The trip was an upfront-quote booking at SGD 22.00. The fare breakdown charged SGD 25.20, made up of the quoted SGD 22.00 plus a SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP line. The GPS trace is complete and clean: 100% coverage, 169 fixes, 10-second sampling, no gaps. Against the gantry coordinates on the fare breakdown (1.3400, 103.7800), the nearest trace fix is 7,482.07 m away at 11:40:50. That is far outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) uses to match a gantry to the trace, so the vehicle did not pass this gantry. The fare breakdown also marks the gantry on_optimal_route=false and the trip record's optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00. The SGD 3.20 is therefore a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4): it is refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction, not as a distance refund. The Driver's own statement that he did not see or pass the gantry agrees with this. The Rider's recovery is the whole SGD 3.20 contested, so the ruling is FULL_REFUND. On the distance question, the trace shows 16.0 km against a 12.5 km optimal route, an excess of 3.5 km or 28%. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gates (0.8 km and 20%) but not the materiality gates (8.0 km and 50%). Because the trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE, POL-RD-11 says no distance-or-time refund is available; the rider is already whole on those lines. I have not applied POL-RD-02. The driver-profile check is not required on a non-material deviation, and even if it were run the driver has 0 deviation flags in 90 days over 610 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern and no POL-RD-06(c) referral exists. The traffic advisory artifact carries no payload, so POL-RD-03 does not exonerate; the chat log contains only the rider's post-trip fare query with no waypoint, so POL-RD-04 does not apply; no amendment timestamps or amended optimal distance are present, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The rider's POL-RD-07 corroboration point is not needed because the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c). No escalation trigger fires: identifiers match, the trace is not impaired, the only unmatched charge is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), and there is no contradictory evidence of comparable strength. Confidence is 0.95. The referral below records the billing-integrity finding required by POL-RD-09(4).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4): billing-integrity finding — refund the SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP charge as an unmatched gantry; the nearest GPS fix is 7,482.07 m from the gantry coordinate, outside the 250 m match radius.

ruling.explanation:
Decision: ESCALATE. No refund issues and no charge is collected or returned at this stage; the contested SGD 5.80 is held for a human reviewer.

What the numbers show. The booked optimal route was 11.0 km and the GPS trace measures 15.0 km, an excess of 4.0 km, or 36.4% (EV-GPS-09115, EV-TRIP-09115). That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (0.8 km absolute and 20% proportional), so on the arithmetic a deviation is established. It does not reach the materiality gates (8.0 km or 50%), so no POL-RD-06 material-deviation uplift arises — and in any event the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists and no conduct referral attaches.

Why no money can move today. The trace is IMPAIRED FOR POLICY PURPOSES under POL-RD-07(a) and (b): a single 160-second gap between consecutive fixes (20:03:10 to 20:05:50) exceeds the 90-second ceiling, and the bounding fixes of that gap are 1.35 km apart, exceeding the 500 m straight-line ceiling. (Limb (c) does not fire — sampling is a steady 10 seconds.) Once the trace is impaired, POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing the deviation on the trace alone; it must be carried by an independent source, and there is none. The chat log carries no driver admission — the driver's only message says his navigation display refreshed and he continued to the destination, and neither message carries a waypoint_hint — so it does not satisfy the limb. No ERP gantry is charged in the fare breakdown that would place the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. The driver's counterparty statement denies an extra stop and a detour request; it is not an admission of the route. And the 15.0 km on the trip record and the fare breakdown is not independent at all: POL-RD-01 says actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy of the same trace measurement, and the billed distance is derived from that trace too. Under POL-RD-07(iii), and mandatorily under POL-RD-10(3), the outcome is therefore ESCALATE and not NO_ACTION, because the missing proof is a data failure rather than a finding for the driver.

What would resolve it. An independent artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names: a driver admission in the chat log, a charged ERP gantry placing the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use, a counterparty admission of the route, or a trip_record.actual_distance_km the platform derived independently of this trace. With one of those, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic would run. On the present figures it recomputes to 20.831 — (3.80 + 0.75 x 11.0 + 0.28 x 22.0) x the 1.1 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee and no ERP or promo — against a charged total of 26.60, a difference of 5.769 that would round up to SGD 5.80. That SGD 5.80 is not awarded today.

Neither party overreached on exoneration, and both are right not to: the only traffic advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-09115-01) carries no payload, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing; no pickup or dropoff amendment exists and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The escalation is terminal: the disputed SGD 5.80 is held rather than collected or refunded, and the fare's payment status and refund-issued figures are left as they are.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee stands on the rider's account, and the driver is paid SGD 3.20, being 80% of that fee under POL-NS-07.

The charge is verified limb by limb under POL-NS-01, as the rider asked. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 08:10:20. (b) The GPS trace places the driver 24.0 m from the pickup pin — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius under POL-NS-02 — from 08:10:00, i.e. before the arrival event; 33 stationary fixes at 0.0 km/h satisfy the three-consecutive-in-radius requirement many times over. (c) The dwell is 320 seconds, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 08:10:00 to the cancellation at 08:15:20, against the 300 second STANDARD minimum; the derived shortfall is -20 seconds, so there is no shortfall and POL-NS-06 has nothing to refund. (d) There is no boarding event, the trip was terminated by the driver at 08:15:20 (after the dwell elapsed) with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which limb (d) recognises. All four limbs hold.

The rider's verification challenge is answered and does not break any limb. His further points do not change the outcome and are accepted as far as they go: his own position is not an ingredient of this charge (POL-NS-06 decides the waiting test 'whether or not the rider was present'), and his device track (a stationary point about 519 m from the pin, no qualifying fix inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius) is therefore not needed either way; he expressly does not press POL-NS-04 and concedes its limb (a) fails, which is correct — every chat message is the system arrival notice or the driver's own; and only the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line is in issue.

Displacing clauses do not fire. POL-NS-05: at the arrival timestamp the driver was 24.0 m from the pin at 0.0 km/h, so the marker is not false and no clock recomputation arises (arrived_at 08:10:20 coincides with a trace fix, so no POL-NS-08(a) skew). POL-NS-03: the whole premise is a driver stationary outside the arrival radius, which is not this case. POL-NS-04: not applicable, as above. POL-NS-06: no shortfall. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09101-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0); that makes POL-NS-06 limb (i) accumulation unavailable by the clause's own terms, but the driver does not rely on it — the single uninterrupted interval already supplies the dwell — and its absence carries no fact in this ruling.

On the money: the fee is the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under fee_schedule.resolution_rule, which equals the fare breakdown's cancellation_fee line of SGD 4.00 and the total charged of SGD 4.00, so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect arises. POL-NS-07 therefore pays the driver 80% of SGD 4.00 = SGD 3.20, with the residual 20% retained as the platform fee. The anti-farming guard does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1/120 completed trips is about 0.008 (below 0.08), so compensation is paid. As POL-NS-07 and POL-GEN-03 require, the disposition of the FEE is that the charge stands as it presently is (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), while the ruling VALUE is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd at SGD 3.20. This is not a second payment or a refund to the filing party.

No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is engaged: confidence is above the 0.70 floor; the artifacts agree on arrival, dwell and timing; the pair shows 0 disputes_with_counterparty_90d each; the anti-farming check does not trip and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0; and no deciding artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)-(d) — the trace has 100% coverage, no gaps and 33 fixes, the chat log's 3 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count, and the fare line reconciles. The deciding facts rest on the GPS trace and the trip record, both at full weight, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and I set confidence at 0.95. No referral arises: POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire because the arrival marker is genuine, and POL-NS-07's escalation branch does not fire. Per POL-GEN-01, no context-only profile field (rating, lifetime counters, prior_no_show_flags and the like) was used as a ground of decision.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Rider and driver: this is a verified no-show. The SGD 6.00 charge stands, and the driver is paid SGD 4.80.

For the rider: your SGD 6.00 charge is not refunded. The driver's GPS trace holds him 24.01 m from the T3 Door 5 ride-hail bay — well inside the 150 m Changi Airport arrival radius — for 51 consecutive fixes from 22:40:00 to 22:48:20, a continuous 500-second hold measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, against the 480-second Airport minimum. His arrival tap at 22:40:20 came after he was already inside the geofence, his recorded speed throughout was 0.0 km/h, and he cancelled at 22:48:20 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the dwell had elapsed. He answered your 'I am walking over now' message 18 seconds later saying he would remain at Door 5, so POL-NS-04 does not apply at limb (b) (it would also fail limb (c): your device's fixes sit 519.47 m from the pin, outside the 200 m presence radius). There is no shortfall for POL-NS-06 to refund (500 s − 480 s = +20 s), the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05, and POL-NS-03's wrong-entrance test does not apply because the driver was inside the radius. Your own claim that the airport is large and the driver cancelled as you walked over is therefore answered by the driver's in-geofence hold of a full 8 minutes 20 seconds.

For the driver: you are compensated SGD 4.80, being 80 percent of the SGD 6.00 fee under POL-NS-07. Your no-show terminations in the trailing 30 days are 1, below the anti-farming threshold of 4, so the payout is not withheld.

On the rider's escalation request: POL-NS-09(b) does not fire. The rider track and the chat log do not contradict each other — a rider reporting he is 'walking over' is consistent with being roughly 519 m from the bay — and rider presence is not the fact that decides this fee, because POL-NS-06 refunds a shortfall whether or not the rider was present and POL-NS-01 turns entirely on the driver's conduct. No other trigger applies: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the repeat-counterparty counters are 0 and 0, and the anti-farming check does not trip.

The driver's statement that he waited more than eight minutes and replied at once is consistent with the trace and the chat, but it is his own account given the next day, adds nothing the instruments do not already show, and carries no weight of its own. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09102-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and is relied on by neither side; it is the only reason POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable, and nothing is asserted against that absent artifact. The lifetime profile counters (rider prior_no_show_flags 1 and prior_disputes_filed 1; driver prior_no_show_flags 2 and prior_deviation_flags 0) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and form no part of this ruling; the counters the clauses do name (rider no_show_disputes_30d 0, disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 for both parties, driver no_show_terminations_30d 1 over completed_trips_30d 120) are clean on both sides.

Figures used: SGD 6.00 cancellation fee = the greater of the Airport zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_PLUS vehicle-tier fee (SGD 6.00), which reconciles to fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee and creates no POL-NS-08(d) defect; compensation SGD 4.80 = 80 percent x SGD 6.00. Confidence 0.90, resting on the full-weight GPS trace and trip record that carry the deciding facts.
